subject: english
learning_objectives: State the rules for doubling a final consonant before adding a suffix
Apply the rules correctly to one-syllable and multi-syllable words
Handle special cases: words ending in -p and -c

sections.heading: Rule 1 – One-syllable words (one vowel + one consonant)
sections.content:
Double the final consonant before a suffix beginning with a vowel.
big→bigger | bat→batting | drop→dropped | drum→drummer

Exception – do NOT double when the vowel is already doubled (digraph):
boat→boating | boil→boiled | cheap→cheapest | sweet→sweeter
Special exception: wool→woollen

sections.heading: Rule 2 – Multi-syllable words: accent on last syllable
sections.content:
Double the final consonant when the stress falls on the last syllable.
ad-MIT→admittance | be-GIN→beginning | for-GET→forgetting | oc-CUR→occurrence

sections.heading: Rule 3 – Multi-syllable words: accent NOT on last syllable
sections.content:
Do NOT double the final consonant.
EN-ter→entering | HAP-pen→happened | IN-habit→inhabitant | RE-fer→reference

sections.heading: Rule 4 – Words ending in -p
sections.content:
A final 'p' is doubled:
handicap→handicapped | kidnap→kidnapped | worship→worshipped
Exception: develop→developed (NOT developped)

sections.heading: Rule 5 – Words ending in -c
sections.content:
Add 'k' before the suffix to preserve the hard /k/ sound:
frolic→frolicked | mimic→mimicked | panic→panicky
